summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)
Maryland - Courts & Judicial Proc. § 3-801 et seq. (CINA—Child in Need of Assistance proceedings)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that a juvenile court may award custody under CJP § 3-819(e) only after sustaining the petition against one parent and finding the other able and willing to care for the child, that the best-interest standard governs the exercise of that discretion, and that the parent must be allowed an evidentiary hearing on material disputes.
key_cases.relevance: It governs the common disposition in which the CINA case is closed with a custody award to the non-offending parent.
key_cases.quote: If those prerequisites are established, the best interest of the child is the standard that applies to the court's decision whether and, if so, how to exercise that discretion

key_cases.citation: No. 1267, Sept. Term 2020 (Md. Ct. Spec. App. July 29, 2021)
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court vacated a CINA adjudication and disposition, holding that at a contested adjudicatory hearing the department must introduce evidence complying with the Maryland Rules, and that findings resting solely on attorney proffers and an unadmitted report are clearly erroneous.
key_cases.relevance: It shows when an adjudication must be undone and the matter reheard rather than allowed to stand.
key_cases.quote: the court's findings of fact at the contested adjudicatory hearing were clearly erroneous because they were based solely on proffers from counsel and the unadmitted Report

key_cases.case_name: Montgomery County Department of Health & Human Services v. P.F.
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an order requiring the agency to reclassify a sexual-abuse finding as 'ruled out' and to expunge its records and central registry entry, where the ALJ found no credible evidence that abuse occurred after a deficient investigation.
key_cases.relevance: It is the administrative analogue of a dismissal, with mandatory record consequences.
key_cases.quote: MCHHS must comply with the order to reclassify the case as "ruled out," and expunge its records and registry.

extended_foster_care_age: Up to the 21st birthday, and only while the young person meets one of five conditions: completing secondary education or a program leading to an equivalent credential; enrolled in an institution providing post-secondary or vocational education; participating in a program or activity designed to promote or remove barriers to employment; employed at least 80 hours per month; or incapable of any of those due to a medical condition documented in the case plan (COMAR 07.02.11.04B). Not eligible for out-of-home placement if married, in the military, or not complying with those conditions (COMAR 07.02.11.04C). Re-entry: the juvenile court has jurisdiction over a former CINA whose commitment to the local department was rescinded after age 18 but before age 20 years 6 months and who did not exit foster care due to reunification, adoption, guardianship, marriage, or uniformed services duty, and that jurisdiction continues until age 21 (Md. Code, Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 3-804(b)(2) and (c)).
